newsitem.title: CAMEROON: Rwanda tribunal official seeks suspect in Cameroon.
newsitem.headline: Rwanda tribunal official seeks suspect in Cameroon.

text.p: The registrar of the International Criminal Tribunal on Rwanda's 1994 massacres arrived in Cameroon on Monday for talks on the handover of a prime suspect, former army colonel Theoneste Bagasora.

Andronico Adede told Reuters that he was hoping to discuss the matter with Cameroon's justice minister. "I also hope that a mission made up, among others, of security agents will come soon to collect Colonel Bagasora," he said by telephone.

Cameroon's courts have ruled that the Tanzania-based tribunal, which is investigating the killing by Hutu hardliners of up to a million minority Tutsis and moderate Hutus, has the right to extradite Bagasora and 11 others held in Cameroon.
They ruled that the U.N. court outranked Cameroon's national courts in international law.
Bagasora was a top official at the defence ministry during the massacres and is one of Rwanda's most wanted men. Cameroon's court declined to rule on a Rwandan extradition request.
Officials say that the handover of Bagasora depends on the go-ahead from President Paul Biya, which they describe as an administrative formality.
The 12 suspects were arrested in March and April.

The Hutu-dominated government which instigated the genocide was defeated in civil war and replaced by a new administration set up by the mainly Tutsi Rwanda Patriotic Front (RPF), whose forces had invaded from neighbouring Uganda in 1990.
An estimated 80,000 Rwandan Hutus have since been arrested on charges of organising or participating in the massacres.
